cards.text: Last time, in Caesarea, the Holy Spirit fell on a whole houseful of Gentiles while Peter was still preaching. Now the news travels, and nobody even needed a group chat. The apostles and brothers throughout Judea hear that the Gentiles also received the word of God.

cards.question: True or false: when Peter goes up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers welcome him with open arms.
The circumcised believers in Jerusalem have a complaint for Peter. What is it?

answers.text: He visited uncircumcised men and ate with them
He baptized people without asking the apostles
He stayed away from Jerusalem far too long

cards.text: So Peter starts at the beginning and walks them through the whole sequence of events. That's more than I ever managed the day somebody asked me why the whole kitchen was full of smoke.
Peter starts in Joppa. He was praying, and in a trance he saw a vision: something let down from heaven by its four corners, coming right down to him.

cards.question: In Peter's vision, what came down from heaven by its four corners?
Peter looked closely at the sheet from heaven. What did he see in it?

cards.text: Then Peter tells them he heard a voice: "Get up, Peter, kill and eat." Friend, if that were me, these eyebrows would've shot straight up into my hat.

cards.question: True or false: when the voice tells Peter to kill and eat, Peter jumps right up and does it.
Peter answers the voice with No Lord. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Nothing impure has ever entered his mouth
He has been fasting since early that morning
He doesn't know whose voice is speaking

cards.question: The voice speaks from heaven a second time: Do not call anything impure that God has made ___.
Peter tells them this whole back-and-forth with the voice happened ___ times.

cards.text: Then everything is drawn back up into heaven. The sheet, the animals, all of it. Gone, like my edges after twenty years of stamping.
Just then, three men sent from Caesarea stop at the house where Peter is staying. JUST THEN. My oven timer has never once been that on time.

cards.question: The Spirit tells Peter what to do about the three men from Caesarea. What is it?
True or false: Peter heads off with the men from Caesarea all by himself.

cards.text: Peter and those six brothers go into the man's home. And the man tells them he saw an angel standing right there in his house.

cards.question: True or false: the man says the angel told him to send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
The angel said Peter would bring a message by which the man and all his household would be ___.

cards.text: Then Peter tells them the big moment. As he began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them. Friend, the man didn't even make it to his second point.

cards.question: Peter says the Holy Spirit fell on the people in that house in a way he recognized. How?

answers.text: Just as He fell on us at the beginning
Only after they were all baptized
Slowly over many days of prayer

cards.text: Right then, Peter remembered something the Lord had said. One of those moments where it all clicks at once.

cards.question: Watching the Holy Spirit fall on that house, what word of the Lord did Peter remember?

answers.text: John baptized with water but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit
Go and make disciples of all nations and baptize them in My name
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved on the last day

cards.text: So Peter lays it out plain. God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Then Peter asks the believers in Jerusalem: who was I to ___ the work of God?
True or false: after hearing Peter out, the believers in Jerusalem keep arguing with him.
Their objections are gone. What do the believers in Jerusalem do instead?

cards.text: And they say it out loud: "So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life." They went from "You ate with WHO?" to glorifying God. Now THAT is a turnaround.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 15 quotes "You ate with WHO?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card tells facts from the previous passage: in Caesarea, the Holy Spirit fell on a houseful of Gentiles while Peter was still preaching (Acts 10:44). It cites only Acts 11:1 and gives no reference for those outside facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "After twenty years of stamping" adds a new fact to Papa Dorin's backstory. The backstory only says "years of good baking" and never gives a number.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. In the text, everything is drawn back up into heaven all at once. Worn-down edges fade slowly over years. The comparison doesn't share the core action of being suddenly taken away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "The man" is Cornelius, a new person, but the card never says who he is. In this passage the text only says "the man's home." The baker is never told it's Cornelius, the Gentile from Caesarea, yet card 14 later uses Cornelius as an answer choice.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Those six brothers" points back to a number the baker was never told. Card 3 only establishes that Peter didn't go alone, so the moment doesn't make sense on its own.

rule.text: A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: On the card before, "the man" meant Cornelius. Here "the man didn't even make it to his second point" means Peter, so it's unclear who is meant.

rule.text: A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Just as He fell on us at the beginning," is in Peter's first-person Bible voice. The wrong answers are plain descriptions. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Acts 11:17 says "So if God gave them the same gift..." The card drops the "if" and states it as a flat statement.
